The answer is still **C**: the son was an intended beneficiary, but his rights had not vested because he had not learned of the contract, relied on it, or accepted it, so the owner and landscaper could modify the payee term. The shared note is wrong, because under Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 311 a beneficiary's rights generally vest on reliance, assent, or suit, not on signing, so the parties could still change the payee. A is wrong because naming the son as payee is not an assignment, and D is wrong because a third-party beneficiary need not give consideration.

CONFIDENCE: 70
